  "text": "A seed fell out, or something shaped like one. It landed in the butter beside the mark her sleeve had made.

“Don't lose that,” she said.

He lifted it with his thumbnail. A small brass screw, black in the groove.

“What's it from?”

“The plate on the door.”

“You've been there.”

She took his knife and scraped the butter from the screw. He watched her wipe the blade against the edge of her toast.

“Not since they put the road through.”

“The house is still there.”

“Yes.”

He turned the envelope over. His name had been written in capitals. The stamp showed a bird he couldn't identify, its feet disappearing into blue water.

“Who sent this?”

She pushed her plate away.

“Your father paid every January. I found the receipts when I was looking for his pension papers.”

“For a room?”

“For keeping it.”

Outside, the neighbour's boy dragged a wheelie bin along the path. One wheel caught on the broken paving, and they listened to him work it loose.

“I thought we could stop paying,” she said.

He laid the photograph beside the key. The pale thing on the gate might have been a bag. It might have been a child's coat, hung by its hood.

“What's in there?”

“I never went down.”

“But you went to the house.”

“To wait for him.”

She stood and carried both plates to the sink. His toast was still on his.

“How long?”

She held the plates under the tap without turning it on.

“Long enough to know he wasn't doing what he said.”"
